*   **Outputs:** A 3D froxel grid (texture) where each cell contains accumulated density, albedo, and emission values derived from all overlapping volumes.
**FogVolume Row Texture:** A 1D texture or buffer where each row represents one visible volume.
The layout includes shape type, transform matrix, material properties (density, color), and noise parameters.
**Fog Density Atlas:** A single 3D texture formed by stacking individual density textures (from NoiseTexture3D or ImageTexture3D) in depth.

*   **Float Texel Upload:** Float texels upload raw as half float because the reference engine gives a float format no sRGB view and WebGL2 always filters a half float.
*   **ShaderMaterial Limitation:** A fog ShaderMaterial runs no fog shader.
*   **Compressed/Integer Formats:** An Image in a block-compressed format draws nothing.
*   **sRGB Decoding:** A 3D colour slot still decodes every texture as sRGB.
*   **Time Complexity:** O(V * F), where V is the number of visible volumes and F is the average number of froxels covered by each volume.
With optimization, F is reduced to only covered froxels.
*   **Memory Complexity:** O(A + G), where A is the size of the density atlas and G is the size of the froxel grid.
*   **Strengths:** Supports complex local fog shapes and variations; integrates with global fog; supports noise-based dynamic fog.
*   **Limitations:** Limited by atlas size (2048 slices); requires careful handling of texture formats; ShaderMaterial integration is non-trivial.
*   **When to use:** When non-uniform, patchy fog effects are needed.
*   **When not to use:** When simple, uniform fog is sufficient; when performance is critical and many volumes are used (due to atlas limits).
Fog Volume Grid Rendering is a technique used in real-time volumetric rendering to integrate local fog volumes into a global froxel-based fog system.
It is commonly used in game engines to create atmospheric effects like fog banks, mist, and layered clouds.
